facts.text: Pre-postseason (Sep 27): The Houston Astros (81–81) became the first team in MLB history to win a division without a winning record, taking the AL West and the No. 3 seed.

Pre-postseason (Sep 14): The Los Angeles Dodgers clinched their 14th straight postseason berth (2013–2026), tying the Braves' NL record streak of 14 (1991–2005, excluding 1994); the Dodgers are the two-time defending champions.

Pre-postseason: The 12-team field was AL Rays (98–64, best AL record), Guardians (85–77 per the postseason page), Astros (81–81), Yankees (93–68), Red Sox (87–75), White Sox (84–78) and NL Brewers (103–59, best record in MLB), Dodgers (100–62), Braves (94–68), Padres (91–71), Cubs (89–73), Phillies (88–74).

Pre-postseason: Both Chicago teams (Cubs and White Sox) made the postseason, only the fourth time ever (1906, 2008, 2020, 2026); the Padres clinched a third straight berth for the first time in franchise history.

Pre-postseason (Sep 11): The Rays clinched their first playoff berth since 2023 on Junior Caminero's walk-off two-run home run against the Astros for a 3–1 win, in their return season to Tropicana Field after Hurricane Milton roof damage.
AL Wild Card Game 1 (Sep 29): The No. 6 seed White Sox beat the No. 3 seed Astros 6–3 at Daikin Park, with Sam Antonacci's RBI double and a Colson Montgomery solo homer helping.

AL Wild Card Game 2 (Sep 30): The White Sox beat the Astros 7–3, led from Kyle Teel's early RBI single, and swept the series 2–0; it was Houston's sixth straight playoff loss dating back to the 2023 ALCS.

AL Wild Card (Sep 30): The White Sox' sweep of the Astros was their first postseason series win since the 2005 World Series (also a sweep of Houston) and sent them to the ALDS for the first time since 2021.
AL Wild Card Game 1 (Sep 29): The Yankees beat the Red Sox 9–0 at Yankee Stadium, with Cam Schlittler pitching six shutout innings.
AL Wild Card Game 2 (Sep 30): The Yankees beat the Red Sox 9–2, with Max Fried throwing six shutout innings and Cody Bellinger and Luis García Jr. homering, completing a 2–0 sweep.

AL Wild Card (Sep 30): The Yankees' sweep was the first postseason series sweep by either team in the history of the Red Sox–Yankees rivalry; New York improved to 4–3 against Boston in postseason series.

NL Wild Card Game 1 (Sep 29): The Braves came back to beat the Phillies 5–3 at Truist Park; Philadelphia led 3–2 after seven innings until Austin Riley hit a three-run homer in the bottom of the eighth.

NL Wild Card Game 2 (Sep 30): The Phillies beat the Braves 4–3 in 10 innings after trailing 3–1 in the eighth; Kyle Schwarber and Bryce Harper hit solo homers to force extras and Alec Bohm's solo homer in the top of the 10th won it.
NL Wild Card Game 3 (Oct 1): The Braves beat the Phillies 6–2 at Truist Park behind home runs from Michael Harris II, Ozzie Albies and Matt Olson to win the series 2–1.

NL Wild Card (Oct 1): Atlanta's series win was its first postseason series victory since the 2021 World Series and the first time it beat the Phillies in four postseason meetings; it was the only 2026 Wild Card series not decided by a sweep.
NL Wild Card Game 1 (Sep 29): The Padres blanked the Cubs 8–0 at Petco Park, with Michael King throwing seven shutout innings.

NL Wild Card Game 2 (Sep 30): The Padres beat the Cubs 4–1 on a two-run single by Xander Bogaerts and a two-run homer by Gavin Sheets, completing the sweep; Cubs pitcher Daniel Palencia then hit Jake Cronenworth with his next pitch, drawing shouts from Padres players.

ALDS Game 1 (Oct 3): The Rays beat the Yankees 1–0 at Tropicana Field as Drew Rasmussen threw eight shutout innings with 10 strikeouts on 101 pitches; Austin Wells' two-out double in the eighth broke up a no-hit bid, and Jonathan Aranda's solo homer off Gerrit Cole was the only run.
ALDS Game 1 (Oct 3): Holding the Yankees to one hit or fewer was a first in franchise postseason history for New York; Bryan Baker closed the game by striking out Giancarlo Stanton.

ALDS Game 2 (Oct 5): The Rays beat the Yankees 5–2 after New York committed three errors in the bottom of the first inning; Cam Schlittler was chased in the fifth, and Ben Rice homered twice for the Yankees.
ALDS Game 3 (Oct 7): The Rays completed a 3–0 sweep with a 4–3 win at Yankee Stadium; Víctor Mesa Jr. hit a go-ahead two-run homer in the sixth and Bryan Baker earned his third save of the series.
ALDS Game 3 (Oct 7): Anthony Volpe's apparent game-tying home run off Griffin Jax in the bottom of the sixth was overturned to a double on review for fan interference, keeping Tampa Bay ahead 4–3.

ALDS (Oct 7): The Yankees' sweep was the first time they were ever swept in a postseason series outside the ALCS or World Series; the Rays reached the ALCS for the first time since 2020 and won their first series since that 2020 pennant.

ALDS Game 1 (Oct 3): The White Sox beat the Guardians 3–0 at Progressive Field on Munetaka Murakami's two-run homer; Grant Taylor struck out the final four batters, and it was Chicago's first postseason shutout win since Game 4 of the 2005 World Series.
ALDS Game 2 (Oct 5): The White Sox beat the Guardians 4–3, taking a 2–0 series lead; Sean Burke pitched 5⅓ innings of one-hit ball, while Gavin Williams struck out 11 over five innings for Cleveland.

ALDS Game 3 (Oct 7): The Guardians beat the White Sox 9–3 at Rate Field as Jo Adell's bases-clearing triple in the third made it 4–1; catcher Patrick Bailey hit Cleveland's first home run of the 2026 postseason.

ALDS Game 4 (Oct 8): The Guardians beat the White Sox 9–5 to force Game 5, scoring five runs in the sixth inning after a José Ramírez two-run homer; the White Sox missed their first chance to clinch a postseason series at home since 1906.
ALDS Game 5 (Oct 10): The Guardians–White Sox series is tied 2–2 with Game 5 scheduled at Progressive Field at 8:00 p.m. ET on Oct 10; no result was available in the sources at snapshot time.

NLDS Game 1 (Oct 3): The Brewers beat the Padres 3–2 at American Family Field on Jackson Chourio's two-run homer and William Contreras' solo homer in the seventh; Ty France's ninth-inning drive hit the roof and was caught, and Pat Murphy joked about thanking Bob Uecker.
NLDS Game 2 (Oct 4): The Brewers walked off the Padres 4–3 when Jackson Chourio hit a two-out, two-run single in the bottom of the ninth off closer Mason Miller to take a 2–0 series lead.

NLDS Game 3 (Oct 6): The Padres beat the Brewers 4–3 at Petco Park on Jake Cronenworth's go-ahead solo homer in the fifth (per game recap), with Michael King earning the save; it extended Milwaukee's postseason road losing streak to 12, matching the MLB record held by the Senators/Twins franchise.

NLDS Game 4 (Oct 7): The Brewers beat the Padres 3–1 to clinch the series 3–1 and advance to their third NLCS in eight years; Garrett Mitchell robbed Manny Machado of a potential game-tying homer in the eighth, and the win snapped Milwaukee's 12-game road postseason losing streak.
NLDS (Oct 7): No team led by more than two runs at any point in the Brewers–Padres series, only the second postseason series in MLB history to do that, after the 1915 World Series.

NLDS Game 1 (Oct 3): The Dodgers beat the Braves 5–3 in 100°F heat, the second-hottest MLB postseason game on record; Tarik Skubal won with six innings and seven strikeouts, and Max Muncy's homer set a franchise record of 17 postseason home runs.
NLDS Game 2 (Oct 4): The Braves beat the Dodgers 3–2 at Dodger Stadium, with Michael Harris II going 3-for-5, to even the series; Max Muncy homered in the ninth to make it 3–2.

NLDS Game 3 (Oct 6): The Dodgers beat the Braves 3–1 at Truist Park as Yoshinobu Yamamoto allowed one run over seven innings with 10 strikeouts; Enrique Hernández and Freddie Freeman homered off Chris Sale (the Wikipedia series page credits Hernández with the two-run homer, the postseason summary names Teoscar Hernández).

NLDS Game 4 (Oct 7): The Dodgers beat the Braves 4–1 to win the series 3–1; Andy Pages hit a go-ahead two-run single in the seventh, Max Muncy homered in the ninth (his third of the series), and Edwin Díaz earned the save.
NLDS Game 4 (Oct 7): Dave Roberts earned his 72nd postseason win as a manager, passing Tony La Russa for second-most in MLB history; the Dodgers reached their third straight NLCS.
NLCS preview (Oct 7): The Brewers and Dodgers meet in the NLCS for the fourth postseason meeting (2018, 2020 and 2025 all won by the Dodgers); Milwaukee holds home-field advantage as the No. 1 seed.

Still alive (Oct 10): Rays (AL) are in the ALCS awaiting the Guardians–White Sox winner; Brewers and Dodgers are set for the NLCS. Eliminated: Astros, Red Sox, Yankees (AL); Cubs, Phillies, Padres, Braves (NL).

upcoming: NLCS Game 1: Dodgers at Brewers, Sun Oct 11, 7:00 p.m. CDT, American Family Field (Brewers hold home field); NLCS is best-of-seven.
ALDS Game 5: White Sox at Guardians, Sat Oct 10, 8:00 p.m. EDT, Progressive Field (series tied 2–2; winner faces the Rays).
ALCS Game 1: opponent TBD (Guardians or White Sox) at Rays, Mon Oct 12, 8:00 p.m. EDT, Tropicana Field.
notes: Primary source is English Wikipedia's 2026 postseason page and its ALDS, NLDS, and Wild Card sub-pages (which cite MLB.com, ESPN and others); direct ESPN/MLB.com/AP recaps were not fetched.
The postseason page marks the ALCS as TBD vs Rays and NLCS 0–0; no LCS games had been played at snapshot.
ALDS Game 5 (CLE–CWS, Oct 10 8 p.m. ET) is unplayed at snapshot; do not assume a winner.
The postseason page says Teoscar Hernández homered in NLDS G3 while the NLDS page says Enrique Hernández; flagged in the fact text.
Wikipedia pages carry a 'current event' banner and may change; the Guardians' regular-season record appears as 85–77 on the postseason page but 85–76 on the ALDS page.
unverified: No second-source (ESPN/MLB.com/AP) confirmation of any fact; all rely on Wikipedia.
